account: Today I have kept my morning office session and have now reached the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, arriving at 10:07. My remaining appointments include lunch at home, council letters, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, and an evening hall inspection arranged for 17:55/18:00 before going home at nineteen. The unusual thing is repeated, identical talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery' from Townsfolk 08, 18, and 28 near town hall. I have heard no actual description of a change, no eyewitness account, and no confirmed difficulty. The neighbour also says there is no confirmed bridge or port change and asked Twenty-eight what they had personally seen. Yesterday's residents' report likewise established no verified complaint about the quay or ferry, though that does not prove everything is well. There may simply be a circulating rumour; I cannot yet tell what it refers to. There are also signs of bread being arranged for gatherings: the neighbour says the baker wants organizers to arrange bread beforehand, the baker publicly offered advance orders, and Townsfolk 08 reported the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread. These could be ordinary supplies for an event, possibly related to the hall arrangements, but I have no evidence connecting them. Freight reportedly remains busy with deliveries. The secretary has been maintaining the appointment books and is now approaching near the mill holding a written book. I suspect there may be activity or gathering plans I have not been told about, but I do not know their purpose or whether anyone is deliberately excluding me. I should distinguish confirmed observations from repeated hearsay while keeping my appointments.
